adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/bug] AssertEvents.java:478 — isAccessTokenId logic is inverted: return false when the shortcut matches, so the matcher only passes tokens with the wrong grant shortcut; should return false on mismatch

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), matchesSafely() returns false when the extracted shortcut equals expectedGrantShortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, so it only matches when the shortcut does NOT match. This inverts the intended logic (should fail on mismatch, not on match). Additionally, the substring indices look off for the 6-char context format used elsewhere (grant shortcut is the last 2 chars), but the inversion alone is a clear correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] AssertEvents.java:477 — off-by-one index: grant shortcut occupies indexes 4–5, so substring(3, 5) reads the wrong characters

adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the encoded context prefix is 6 chars: sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShortcut(2) as produced by `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`. That means the grant shortcut occupies indices `[4,6)` (0-based), but the matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which extracts the wrong characters (last char of tokenType + first char of grant). This makes the matcher incorrect for the new token id format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit — no validation that getShortcut() returns exactly 2 chars; custom grants with other-length shortcuts silently break the hard-coded 6-char prefix parsing and brick token decoding

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes token-id context parsing to a 6-char prefix in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(): it throws if encodedContext.length() != 6 and then slices the grant shortcut as substring(4,6). However, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() (new SPI method) is not constrained to 2 characters (its Javadoc even suggests “usually like 3-letters shortcut”), and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() only checks uniqueness, not length. If a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returns a shortcut of length != 2, encodeTokenId() will emit a non-6-char prefix and decoding will fail at runtime, effectively breaking token-id decoding for those tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut — concurrent first-encounters of unknown grants/shortcuts can interleave puts, leaving the two shared ConcurrentHashMaps temporarily inconsistent and decoding ids incorrectly during that window

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, getShortcutByGrantType() reads/updates only grantsToShortcuts (and opportunistically also grantsByShortcuts), while getGrantTypeByShortcut() reads/updates only grantsByShortcuts (and also updates grantsToShortcuts). Although the two ConcurrentHashMaps are updated via two separate puts (non-atomic across maps), the code never relies on a cross-map invariant for a single operation: each method re-checks the same map it will return from after its refresh attempt. The claimed outcome (“decoding ids incorrectly during that window”) is not demonstrated by the diff; at worst, concurrent first-encounters can cause redundant refresh work, not incorrect decoding attributable to temporary map inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId — throws IllegalStateException for unknown grantType, aborting token issuance for all access tokens in that flow instead of skipping encoding

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` throws `IllegalStateException` when `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` returns null, and `TokenManager.initToken()` now always encodes the access token ID (so such an exception would abort token creation). However, the diff also sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` in the main grant flows (`OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, refresh in `validateToken`, token exchange, etc.), and when the attribute is missing `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` falls back to `UNKNOWN` (`na`), which is explicitly mapped. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that any real flow will produce an unmapped/unknown grantType that triggers the exception; it’s more of a robustness/compatibility concern than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId — throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown shortcuts, surfacing 500s during introspection/userinfo instead of treating the ID as unparseable/legacy

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException when any parsed shortcut is unknown (sessionType/tokenType/grantType), e.g. `if (st == null) { throw ... }` and similarly for `tt` and `gt`. However, the claim that this will “surface 500s during introspection/userinfo” is not verifiable from this PR diff because no call sites for `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` in introspection/userinfo paths are shown. This is therefore a robustness/backwards-compatibility concern (e.g., tokens containing shortcuts from removed/changed providers) grounded in the new logic, but not a demonstrable broken behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken — now public static and used by the encoder, but reads session.getContext().getClient() which is null in non-HTTP contexts, causing NPE; contract not documented/defended for the new caller

adjudication.rationale: Diff makes `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(KeycloakSession)` `public static` and it unconditionally dereferences `session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...)` (no null-check). The new encoder caller (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`) invokes it during token ID encoding, expanding the call surface beyond protocol mappers. While the diff doesn’t prove `session.getContext().getClient()` will be null in some runtime paths, the lack of a defensive check / documented precondition is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern introduced by the new usage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest — missing tests for rawTokenId containing a colon, encodeTokenId round-trip via factory postInit-registered grants, and duplicate-shortcut validation in postInit

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider/Factory (token-id parsing with ':' separator; grant shortcut maps populated in postInit via provider factories; duplicate-shortcut detection in postInit). The new unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only hardcodes grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and exercises basic parse/encode, but does not cover (a) rawTokenId values containing additional ':' characters (parsing uses indexOf(':') in getTokenContextFromTokenId), (b) round-trip behavior when shortcuts are registered via DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), or (c) the duplicate-shortcut validation branch (map size mismatch check) in postInit. These are specific, diff-grounded test gaps rather than a demonstrated functional defect.
